side_a: five packs state that no price row exists anywhere, and the hub cards repeat it
side_b: data/nfl_f4/price_snapshots.csv holds 448 populated number cells cited to a third-party carrier (sports.core.api.espn.com=448), each carrying snapshot_type=open and close for the same game — real market prices, with a status column that reads 'verified'
computed: 309921cc: cells opening_price=0; closing_price=0; hosts no url cited; labels none given | 67233566: cells no populated number cell; hosts no url cited; labels role: open×65, close×65 | 6cefc476: cells our_number=78; market_number=0; hosts (ours, labelled)=78; labels none given | 8362b702: cells no populated number cell; hosts no url cited; labels none given | d966f630: cells opening_number=144; closing_number=157; hosts github.com=262; www.nfl.com=39; labels opening_class: retrospective_reconstruction×132, prior_session_publication×39 | closing_role: open_and_close_final×132, close_provisional×39 | f4: cells line=112; price_american=168; price_decimal=168; hosts sports.core.api.espn.com=448; labels none given — totals: third-party market cells 448, own-labelled 78, repo reconstruction 262, official-cited 39
what_it_changes: This is the price-data policy the brief demands be decided before any backtest is published, and the site answers it two ways at once. One pack has operator open/close pairs (third-party quotes, not official, and its own flags say 13 of 14 games had no settled close); the other five stores are blank or hold our own model number with an official page cited as input provenance. A CLV or ROI figure computed from the first class and described using the second class's language would be a category error — and 'verified' on a third-party quote contradicts the project's own rule that verified means read from an official source.
action: decide the accepted price class in one sentence (official only / licensed vendor / third-party-with-provenance), then relabel what does not qualify and re-point the gates at the surviving rows; if third-party quotes are accepted, they become the earliest usable market reference the project has

subject: A number cell that cites a page which cannot contain it
side_a: data/nfl_d966f630/price_snapshots_open_close.csv: 39 populated number cells whose own *_source_url points at an nfl.com schedule page — a page that prints fixtures, times and scores, never a line — that exact URL was read in full this session (R10), which is what turns this from an inference about a route name into a tested citation
side_b: the same file's own labels: opening_class='retrospective_reconstruction' or 'prior_session_publication', closing_role='open_and_close_final' or 'close_provisional', and a movement_note that says the two numbers come from two different model versions
computed: populated number cells by cited host: github.com=262; www.nfl.com=39; own labels on those rows: opening_class: retrospective_reconstruction×132, prior_session_publication×39 | closing_role: open_and_close_final×132, close_provisional×39
what_it_changes: Read carefully, this is not a fabricated market price — the pack says in its own note that both numbers are ours. The defect is the citation: a source URL that appears beside a number will be quoted later without the note attached, and 'nfl.com' beside a price-looking number reads as if the league published it. Any residual-against-market column inherits that ambiguity. It is also the case a required-field alarm should catch: the cited host cannot contain the class of value stored.
action: in the owning pack: move the input-provenance URL to an inputs column and leave the number's own source blank (or point it at the model-version file that produced it); add the host-class check to the verifier pattern used here (rule 6)
